iut_type: RF test report internal QC review -- resolving an apparent test-log discrepancy by deferring to the registered/inherited ICS declaration
customer_question: (Internal QC review, not a customer question.) The CTS (Conformance Test Spec) states that if 3Mbps is supported, measurement should also be taken at 3-DH1 -- based on the test log, it looks like the device supports 3Mbps. Should the 3-DH1 measurement have been included?
question_variants: How should a reviewer resolve an apparent mismatch between what a raw test log seems to show and what the registration's declared ICS states?
actual_issue: During internal QC review of an RF test report, a reviewer noticed the test log appeared to show 3Mbps support, which per the Conformance Test Spec would require an additional 3-DH1 measurement -- raising the question of whether that measurement had been improperly omitted.
plain_english_explanation: The apparent discrepancy was resolved by checking the Test Plan: this registration's RF ICS, inherited from the referenced RF registration, does NOT actually declare 3Mbps support. Since the conformance requirement for an additional 3-DH1 measurement only applies when 3Mbps support is actually declared in the ICS, the registered ICS declaration -- not a superficial read of the test log -- is the authoritative source for determining whether that additional measurement requirement applies. In this case, no additional measurement was needed despite the test log's appearance, because the inherited ICS confirms 3Mbps is not a supported, declared feature for this registration.
consultant_answer: As noted in the Test Plan, the RF ICS inherited from the referenced RF registration does not support 3Mbps for this case -- so the additional 3-DH1 measurement requirement (which only applies when 3Mbps support is declared) doesn't apply here, regardless of what the test log might appear to show.
decision_logic: When a test report reviewer notices an apparent conformance requirement triggered by what the test log seems to show (e.g., evidence of a specific data rate or feature), verify against the registration's actual declared/inherited ICS in the Test Plan before concluding a measurement was improperly omitted -- the ICS declaration, not the raw test log's appearance, determines which conformance requirements actually apply.
final_recommendation: Train report reviewers to cross-check apparent test-log-driven conformance triggers against the registration's actual ICS declaration in the Test Plan, since visual impressions from a test log can be misleading if the underlying registration doesn't actually declare the feature in question.
risk_if_done_wrong: A reviewer who concludes a measurement was improperly omitted based solely on the test log's appearance, without checking the actual ICS declaration, could trigger unnecessary report rework or incorrectly flag a compliant report as deficient.
